1.explanation: The root cause lives in SetColorHandler.postExecute: when an element has an external label (element.labelTarget is truthy), the handler always picks di['background-color'] (fill) to update the label’s color property. To fix the bug, this branch should use di['border-color'] (stroke) when updating external labels so that they match the stroke color rather than the fill color.
1.bug_scenario:
When using the modeling.setColor API on an element that has an external label (e.g. a circle or sequence flow with a separate text label), the handler applies the “background‐color” (fill) to the label’s DI color property. As a result, the external label text is rendered in the fill color (very light orange in the screenshot), instead of the darker stroke color used by embedded labels. This makes the label hard to read.

In the provided screenshot you can see two circles connected by a task, labeled “foo” and “bar”. After setting the color to orange, the shapes use an orange border, but the external text labels are rendered in a pale orange (fill) rather than the bold orange (stroke).
